corrections.why: The Register says the site is closed to public access, and the directory lists it as not accessible to the public. No source mentions a permit process.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com give about 1935. Forest Lookouts quotes agency letters from 1939 and 1940 describing a project to buy and erect an Eagle Butte tower, with erection more than half done by June 1940. The letters also mention an 80-foot tower bought for Shitike Butte in 1935. The sources do not explain the difference, so the story reports both dates.

The Bulletin, quoted on Forest Lookouts, reported seven lightning blazes on August 5, 1974. A 2024 Madras Pioneer retrospective recalls four blazes started within minutes. The story reports both counts.

notes_for_editor: Five page reads and two searches. The build date is the main open question: NHLR and firelookout.com say about 1935, while the agency letters transcribed by Forest Lookouts describe a 1939-1940 purchase and erection, which suggests the 1935 date may be wrong. Reported as a conflict, not resolved. Height 107 ft (32.6 m) agrees across NHLR and firelookout.com. Elevation: NHLR gives 3,168 ft (966 m), firelookout.com and the directory 3,175 ft; the brief's 965.6 m is the NHLR figure and is not in facts. Current status is taken from the Cheryl Hill directory (listed as of July 2026, which warns it may be out of date) and firelookout.com (undated staffing claim). The Madras Pioneer retrospective quotes a line saying the forest service still provided lookouts for three towers in the McQuinn Strip, which does not clearly apply to Eagle Butte, so it is not cited. A 1992 Spilyay Tymoo OCR page mentions a lookout at Eagle Butte, but the OCR is too garbled to quote. No photos added. The 2026 Bench Fire news on the reservation does not mention Eagle Butte in the pages read, so no damage claim is made.
